answer: A raven token functions as a non-transferable routing credit that decays unless forwarded at a strict pulse interval into a distinct island subnet, forcing each identity to maintain its own exclusive network partition. Because a new raven can only be minted by consuming an existing one plus a dynamic fee scaling with total active islands, an attacker pays an exponentially increasing cost per extra fake, since each new puppet requires its own isolated subnet and a freshly consumed token to sustain the forwarding cadence.
